title: Shania Twain’s ‘Little Miss Twain’: Every Track, Ranked
summary: Billboard ranks all 15 songs on Shania Twain's first album since 2023.
contentText:
On her new studio album, Little Miss Twain (out July 24 on Republic Nashville), Shania Twain offers up vivid storylines and revisits some of the defining moments that marked her ascent to one of country music’s most impactful female stars.

Throughout the new project, the five-time Grammy winner is in reflective mode, taking listeners into memories from her childhood growing up in Ontario, Canada, and into her youthful ambitions of leaving Canada in search of musical stardom in Nashville. Twain’s road to Music City was marked by both tragedy and hardships, including the deaths of her parents in a car accident in 1987, and the ensuing necessity of raising her three younger siblings. On the autobiographical Little Miss Twain , songs such as “Northern Town” and the title track pull back the curtain on some of her passage.

Twain’s 1995 sophomore album, The Woman in Me , skyrocketed her popularity, becoming the first of three consecutive albums by Twain to be certified Diamond by the RIAA. Her 1997 blockbuster Come on Over became one of the best-selling albums of all time and spawned three top 10 hits on the Billboard Hot 100: “You’re Still the One,” “That Don’t Impress Me Much” and “From This Moment On.” Recently, the country legend checked off another long-held career ambition, playing at the Toronto-area, approximately 500-capacity The Horseshoe Tavern — a gig that had eluded Twain as a child first making her way in the industry.

Beyond songs that revisit her career progression, Little Miss Twain is filled with songs of love and heartbreak, as well as more light-hearted fare. Twain also has some help on the album, courtesy of guest artists as wide-ranging as The War and Treaty, Tanya Tucker and Queens of the Stone Age frontman Josh Homme.

Twain’s new album doubles down on the songwriting that has been at the heart of her biggest hits and deepest album cuts over the years, while still weaving together elements of country, pop, soul and rock in a way that has become her signature. Below, Billboard ranks all 15 tracks on the album.
